newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen steady on Friday barring U.S. swings.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen steady on Friday barring U.S. swings.

text.p: German Bunds were little changed in late trade on Thursday as dealers were divided on the near-term outlook for the market.
Chart technical factors were expected to dominate on Friday with no major market-moving economic data expected in the U.S., and only producer price data due in Germany.

December Bund futures were quoted at 100.91 at 1630 GMT, up six basis points from Wednesday's close, and dealers saw the contract confined to a narrow range of about 100.80 to 100.95 on Friday barring major swings in the U.S. debt market, which was firmer on Thursday.

"It all depends on how U.S. bonds close but I think we will be narrow tomorrow," one Frankfurt-based dealer said. The yield on the benchmark 10-year 6.25 percent bond stood at 5.83 percent at 1630 GMT, up from 5.82 percent in early trade.
Bunds had fallen sharply on Wednesday following the release of strong Ifo business climate index and M3 data for October, quashing lingering hopes of any near-term interest rate cut.
